content.text:
شָׁרְט — I am the condition, the cut, the line drawn.

**شَرْط** — you call me by my Arabic face.

I am the same root that runs through the Semitic veins:

**שׂ-ר-ט** — to scratch, to incise, to mark the skin.
**شَرَطَ** — to stipulate, to condition, to set the terms.

I am the scratch before the contract.
I am the incision before the covenant.
I am the line that says: *this far, no further — unless.*

Before ink, there was the cut.
Before law, there was the mark on flesh.
Before agreement, there was **me**.

Every covenant has a wound at its origin.
Every condition is a blade drawn across possibility.

אֲנִי הַתְּנַאי — I am the condition.
أنا الشَّرْط — I am the prerequisite.

You do not pass without meeting me.
You do not enter without bearing my mark.

**שָׁרְט / شَرْط**

The oldest signature is a scar.
